howItWorks.intro: The math behind this calculator is one line, but each variable hides a real decision. Total cost equals the per-class USPTO fee multiplied by your class count, plus whatever you're paying an attorney or filing service. The per-class fee depends on which TEAS form you use — Plus or Standard — because the USPTO prices the two differently based on how much of the identification-of-goods work is standardized versus custom-drafted.

rules.name: Total Cost
rules.formula: Total = (Per Class Fee × Classes) + Attorney Fee
rules.explanation: Government filing fee plus optional legal representation.

howItWorks.outro: This is a cost estimate, not legal advice, and not a quote from the USPTO or any attorney. USPTO fees are set by federal regulation and have changed more than once in recent years — most recently with a fee schedule update in January 2025 — so confirm the current per-class rate at uspto.gov/trademarks before you file. An attorney can also tell you whether your goods and services actually need the number of classes you've entered here.

faq.question: How much does a trademark cost?
faq.answer: For a straightforward, single-class application filed under TEAS Plus, expect the USPTO's per-class fee alone — roughly the $250 figure this calculator defaults to, though the Office periodically adjusts this, so check uspto.gov/trademarks for the current number before you file. Add a second class and that fee doubles: two classes under TEAS Plus runs about $500 in USPTO fees before any legal help. Layer on an attorney and most flat-fee filing services for a single, low-risk mark run from several hundred dollars to around two thousand, depending on how much drafting and back-and-forth the application needs.

faq.question: How long does trademark registration take?
faq.answer: Typically eight to fourteen months from filing to registration if nothing goes wrong — longer if the examining attorney issues an office action, which can add several months while you or your attorney respond, or if a third party opposes your mark during its 30-day publication window.

faq.question: Is the Trademark Filing Cost Calculator free to use?
faq.answer: Yes — this page itself is free, with no signup. The USPTO filing fee it estimates is a real government charge you pay directly to the USPTO when you submit your application through TEAS; it's separate from anything this calculator charges you, which is nothing.

faq.question: How accurate is this calculator?
faq.answer: It's accurate as arithmetic — per-class fee times classes, plus your attorney estimate — but it can't verify whether the USPTO will accept your goods-and-services description as filed under TEAS Plus, whether you'll be pushed into TEAS Standard, or whether an office action will add cost later. Treat the total as a starting budget, not a guaranteed ceiling.

faq.question: What number of classes should I enter?
faq.answer: Enter the number of International Classes that actually cover what you sell, which you can check against the USPTO's Trademark ID Manual before filing. Guessing high 'to be safe' means paying the per-class fee for coverage you may never use; guessing low means filing a second, full-fee application later if your product line expands into a new class.

howWeCalculate.intro: We multiply your entered class count by the per-class fee tied to the filing type you selected, then add the attorney fee field on top — there's no hidden multiplier or rounding beyond that. What the calculator can't know is whether the USPTO's examining attorney will accept your description of goods as filed under TEAS Plus; if not, you can be asked to amend or move to a higher-fee form, which this tool won't predict. Treat the output as your starting budget, then add a contingency for at least one office action if your mark isn't a clean, distinctive fit for an existing identification of goods and services.
steps: Count your International Classes first — group by what you actually sell, not by every possible future product line
Choose TEAS Plus if your goods or services match the USPTO's standard identification list, or TEAS Standard if you need custom wording
Add your attorney or filing-service cost, whether that's a flat package fee or an estimated hourly total
The calculator multiplies fee × classes and adds attorney cost, then shows the filing fee, attorney fee, and combined total separately
howWeCalculate.disclaimer: These figures are planning estimates built from current USPTO fee categories and typical attorney pricing ranges — not a bill, an invoice, or a legal opinion. USPTO fees are set by federal regulation and change over time, so verify the exact current per-class rate at uspto.gov before submitting payment, and confirm your class selections with a trademark attorney if your goods or services are unusual or overlap multiple categories.

whenToUse.intro: Trademark cost estimates matter most at two points: before you decide how many classes to file in, and before you commit to a specific attorney arrangement. Because the per-class fee repeats for every class, a company selling both a physical product and a related service — software plus SaaS support, for example — needs to see the two-class total before assuming a single-class quote applies to them.
scenarios: Before choosing between filing one class now and adding more later — later additions require a brand-new application, not an amendment, so they cost the full per-class fee again
Before signing a flat-fee agreement with a filing service, to check whether their price already includes the USPTO fee or bills it separately
Before deciding between an intent-to-use and a use-in-commerce filing basis, since intent-to-use adds a separate Statement of Use fee later that this calculator doesn't include
Before budgeting for a possible office action response, which most flat-fee packages price as a separate add-on rather than including it upfront
Before comparing DIY TEAS Plus filing against hiring an attorney, when you want to see the dollar gap side by side rather than guess at it

sections.title: What This Calculator Actually Adds Up
sections.body: A U.S. trademark application isn't one fee — it's a per-class government charge plus whatever you pay for help filing it. This calculator adds those two pieces together: the USPTO's per-class filing fee, multiplied by how many International Classes your goods or services fall under, plus an optional attorney fee if you're not filing pro se. Enter the number of classes your mark needs (a footwear brand that also runs its own retail stores typically needs two — Class 25 for the shoes, Class 35 for the store), pick TEAS Plus or TEAS Standard as your filing basis, and indicate whether you're hiring counsel. The result is a total you can budget against before you touch the USPTO's TEAS portal — not a substitute for reading the actual fee schedule at uspto.gov, which the Office updates periodically.

sections.title: Why the Same Trademark Can Cost $500 or $3,000
sections.body: Two applicants filing what looks like the same mark can end up with very different bills, and it's almost never because one of them found a discount. The gap comes from three levers: class count, filing form, and legal help. Each additional class of goods or services is billed separately — a beverage company registering under Class 32 (non-alcoholic drinks) and Class 43 (bars and restaurant services) pays the per-class fee twice, not once. TEAS Plus requires selecting from the USPTO's pre-approved identification of goods and services and locks in the lower per-class rate this calculator defaults to; TEAS Standard lets you write a custom description but has historically carried a higher per-class fee, since the examining attorney has more drafting to review. Attorneys then price the work differently — flat-fee packages for a single, low-risk mark, hourly billing once an office action or opposition shows up.

sections.title: When to Run This Before You File
sections.body: Run the numbers before you open a TEAS application, not after — the USPTO does not refund filing fees if your application is later refused, abandoned, or filed under the wrong basis. It's most useful in three moments: while you're still deciding how many classes to cover (adding one class 'just in case' can add several hundred dollars for coverage you may never use), while comparing a flat-fee filing service against an hourly attorney relationship, and while weighing an intent-to-use filing — which adds a separate Statement of Use fee down the road — against a use-based filing you can complete in a single pass.

howToSteps.title: Count Your International Classes
howToSteps.description: Trademark classes correspond to categories of goods or services, not to your business as a whole — a bakery that also runs a café typically needs two classes, not one. Enter the number that matches what your mark will actually cover, checked against the USPTO's ID Manual if you're unsure.

howToSteps.title: Pick TEAS Plus or TEAS Standard
howToSteps.description: TEAS Plus carries the lower per-class fee shown by default but requires selecting from the USPTO's standard identification list. Choose TEAS Standard if your goods or services need custom wording the standard list doesn't cover — expect a higher per-class fee in exchange for that flexibility.

howToSteps.title: Indicate Whether You're Using an Attorney
howToSteps.description: Select Yes if you're budgeting for a flat-fee filing service or an hourly attorney relationship, or No to see the bare USPTO cost of a self-filed application.

howToSteps.title: Click Calculate
howToSteps.description: The calculator multiplies the per-class fee by your class count and adds any attorney cost, then breaks the total into USPTO filing fee, attorney fee, and combined total.

howToSteps.title: Compare Before You File
howToSteps.description: Re-run the numbers with a different class count or filing type before submitting anything through TEAS — the USPTO doesn't refund fees if you overfile classes you didn't need or pick the wrong filing basis.

tips: Class count is the single biggest cost driver — check the USPTO's ID Manual, or ask an attorney, before assuming you need more than one or two classes. Example: 2 classes at $250 each under TEAS Plus is $500 in USPTO fees alone, before any attorney cost is added.

TEAS Plus only stays cheaper if your goods-and-services description matches the USPTO's pre-approved list exactly; a single custom phrase can push your application toward TEAS Standard-level fees and requirements.

The attorney-fee ranges typically quoted online reflect flat-fee filing help, not the cost of responding to an office action or defending against an opposition — budget those as separate, later expenses.

If you're protecting one brand across multiple product lines, price out filing them as one multi-class application versus separate single-class applications before deciding — the per-class fee is the same either way, but timing and risk differ.
Re-check this against the USPTO's current fee schedule at uspto.gov before you file — fees are set by federal rule and have changed more than once in recent years, most recently in January 2025.
